top_stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited BeyondTrust Zero-Day to Take Over Remote Support Servers
top_stories.summary: A China-linked cyber espionage group tracked as Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS 9.3) in BeyondTrust Remote Support servers in late August 2026. The flaw involves improper origin validation in an internal messaging component and allowed attackers to take over Remote Support servers.

top_stories.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup Credential Abuse: 173 M365 Tenants Compromised in Trust-Through-Defaults Incident
top_stories.summary: Threat actors abused a vendor-managed credential in ConnectWise Cloud Backup to authenticate across 173 Microsoft 365 tenants in a supply chain-style attack. The incident highlights failures in credential management and cross-tenant trust, with customer-side controls like MFA and conditional access reportedly ineffective due to the trusted vendor credential context.

top_stories.title: Nine Identity-Layer Bypasses in Twenty-One Days: The Trust-Through-Defaults Pattern Has Reached Every Layer of the Stack
top_stories.summary: Nine distinct identity-layer bypasses were disclosed across multiple tiers of the authentication stack within a 21-day window between late September and mid-October 2026. Each vulnerability exploited a shared structural flaw where receiving systems incorrectly assumed that assertions from trusted sources were valid without further verification, a pattern described as "trust-through-defaults."

top_stories.title: Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack
top_stories.summary: ConnectWise shut down customer access to its Cloud Backup service after hackers accessed application identities and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants through a supply-chain attack. The breach involved the exploitation of application identities, directly impacting Microsoft 365 tenant security for affected ConnectWise customers.

top_stories.title: ConnectWise suspends Cloud Backup service after attackers abuse its Microsoft 365 access
top_stories.summary: ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup service (formerly SkyKick) after attackers used compromised application credentials to access customer Microsoft 365 accounts. The incident also led to suspension of related SaaS Security and Cloud Management services due to their integration with the affected application identity infrastructure.

news.title: Your frontline workers have a workaround for that MFA prompt
news.summary: A Sapio Research survey of 700 IT and security decision-makers found that 95% observed frontline workers bypassing MFA through credential sharing, persistent sessions, and other workarounds in the past 12 months. The research focuses on authentication challenges specific to healthcare and manufacturing environments where shared workstations and workflow pressures conflict with standard MFA implementations.

news.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
news.summary: ConnectWise disabled cloud backups after attackers reportedly used ConnectWise credentials to authenticate into Microsoft 365 tenants. Customer impact remains unconfirmed according to ConnectWise, while researchers indicate downstream MSPs may be affected.

news.title: Inside the Underground Market for Know Your Client Services
news.summary: Cybercriminals are selling underground services including forged identity documents, deepfake videos, and live verification assistance to bypass Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification checks. Flare's research examines the techniques used to create fraudulent verified accounts, targeting identity verification systems used by financial and other regulated industries.

news.title: Cybercriminals favor Microsoft over Apple and Google in brand phishing attacks
news.summary: Check Point Research found Microsoft accounted for 33% of brand impersonation attempts in Q3 2026, up from 23% the previous quarter and roughly four times the share of any other brand. Apple and Google each followed at 8%, with attackers targeting Microsoft credentials due to their broad access potential across enterprise systems.

news.title: GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories
news.summary: The GhostAction threat actor has expanded its supply chain attack campaign to include credential stealer malware disguised as a font file, planted across 94 GitHub repositories. The attack targets open-source developers through phishing and malicious GitHub Actions workflows, with the stealer designed to harvest credentials from compromised systems.

news.title: IDWolf
news.summary: IDWolf is a read-only PowerShell-based auditing tool for Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID hygiene assessment. It offers deterministic findings, attack path analysis, compliance mapping for NIS2/ISO 27001/DORA/GDPR, and supports HTML/CSV/JSONL reporting with optional AI analysis.

news.title: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup After Attackers Compromise Microsoft 365 Tenants
news.summary: ConnectWise disabled seven application identities after threat actors gained unauthorized access to them and used them to compromise Microsoft 365 tenants. The incident led ConnectWise to suspend its Cloud Backup service while the investigation continues.

news.title: SAP Cloud SDK for Python Lets Attackers Steal OAuth2 Credentials Through a Tenant Subdomain Input — CVSS 10.0
news.summary: A CVSS 10.0 Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability in the SAP Cloud SDK for Python allows attackers to steal OAuth2 client credentials by manipulating the tenant_subdomain parameter without authentication. The flaw enables hijacking of OAuth2 token requests, exposing application client IDs and secrets.

news.title: Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
news.summary: Threat actors used a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential to gain unauthorized access to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants belonging to managed service providers' customers. The attack highlights risks associated with delegated administrative credentials and third-party service provider access to M365 environments.

news.title: The Industry’s Primary Agent Identity Standard Expires in 36 Days
news.summary: The ID-JAG (Identity for Autonomous Agents) draft standard is set to expire on November 22, with 36 days remaining as of October 17, 2026. The expiration highlights a gap between commercially deployed agent identity infrastructure and the pace of institutional standards development.

news.title: Mage OSS Ships an OAuth Bypass That Creates Sessions from Unrecognized Providers — the Tenth Trust-Through-Defaults Incident in Twenty-One Days
news.summary: Mage OSS has been found to contain a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-111823, CVSS 9.8) that creates sessions from unrecognized OAuth providers, affecting all versions through 0.9.80. The flaw is tracked under GHSA-93gm-r5p2-wxq7 and represents a trust-through-defaults misconfiguration in OAuth session handling.

news.title: Microsoft Is Blocking Every Third-Party Script from Its Entra Sign-In Page — and It Hits Mid-October
news.summary: Microsoft will enforce Content Security Policy (CSP) on Entra sign-in pages at login.microsoftonline.com starting mid-to-late October 2026, blocking all third-party scripts not from trusted Microsoft domains. The change is part of Microsoft's Secure Future Initiative and will affect organizations that inject custom scripts into Entra sign-in pages.

news.title: Six Vendors Are Shipping Agent Identity Products. The IETF Has Not Finished the Standard.
news.summary: Six vendors are shipping agent identity products despite the IETF's ID-JAG standard remaining an unfinished Internet-Draft (version -04, expiring November 22). This creates a standardization gap where commercial implementations of agent identity are proceeding ahead of the formal specification they would rely on.

news.title: The IETF Is Formalizing the Identity Layer Vendors Are Already Shipping
news.summary: The IETF is formalizing standards for an identity layer designed to support autonomous AI agents, addressing governance gaps as agent deployments scale rapidly. The standardization effort covers the technical infrastructure needed to authenticate and authorize non-human identities, an area where vendors have already begun shipping implementations.

news.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
news.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support has been exploited, joining a wave of edge device vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks. BeyondTrust is a PAM vendor whose remote support and privileged access products are widely deployed in enterprise environments.

news.title: UAT-11985 Uses Fake Event Invites to Target Taiwan Research Affiliates With Google AitM Phishing
news.summary: Researchers have disclosed details of an APT spear-phishing campaign (UAT-11985) targeting Taiwan research organization affiliates using adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) techniques to steal Google account credentials and MFA codes. The campaign employs fake event invites to bypass MFA protections by intercepting authentication tokens in real time.

news.title: Keeper Security and Tenable Integrate to Streamline Cloud Risk Detection, Remediation and Vulnerability Assessment
news.summary: Keeper Security and Tenable have announced a product integration connecting Keeper's identity security platform with Tenable's cloud risk and vulnerability assessment tools. The integration enables remediation of cloud security findings and secures privileged credentials used during vulnerability scanning.

news.title: jumpserver v5.1.0
news.summary: JumpServer has released version 5.1.0 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides DevOps and IT teams with secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, Database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser.

news.title: Ivanti ICS Zero-Day Attacks Highlight Vendor Patching Hurdles
news.summary: A high-severity zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-104935) in Ivanti ICS combines authentication bypass and remote code execution, and was only partially discovered and patched in July. The incomplete patch left a window for threat actors to exploit the authentication bypass flaw, highlighting challenges in fully remediating complex vulnerabilities in enterprise access infrastructure.

news.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat
news.summary: A vulnerability dubbed "SneakPeek" in Anthropic's Claude Code Desktop allows attackers to steal credentials silently via the application's preview pane without any user interaction. The flaw can expose sensitive authentication material including SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and OAuth tokens through a zero-click attack vector.

news.title: Zero-Days Lurk in Microsoft's Overgrown October Patch Tuesday
news.summary: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday, described as the largest security update ever, contains multiple zero-day vulnerabilities including defense bypasses and unauthenticated remote code execution flaws. The update includes security fixes relevant to IAM professionals managing Microsoft environments and authentication infrastructure.

news.title: No Identity, No Recovery: Cyber Resilience Starts With IAM
news.summary: The article argues that identity and access management is foundational to cyber resilience, particularly given the proliferation of enterprise apps and cloud identity providers. The piece calls for a rethink of identity security strategy in modern enterprise environments.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited with accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to keep up with testing and deploying the volume of fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, with evidence pointing to a Louisiana-based identity verification company as the source of the leaked images. The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the breach, which affects identity verification infrastructure used broadly across the U.S. and Canada.
